Attendance (10%)

Assignment (30%)
Order imbalance multiple regression project.
The content is very easy if you have completed ISOM 4530 project. Even you have not, 80% of codes are copy and paste from lecture python file.
However, I got no idea why professor said it is so difficult and then remove one part of the project (waste my time to do Task 4 lol)
The key is that you need to use apply / rolling well and then it is very easy.

Still, if you know nothing, you should go to the tutorial sessions since TA basically write nearly all the codes for you (as far as I know)

Final Exam (60%) with double sided cheat sheet
1 hour is so rush for these 30 MC. Do not fake by the sample exam, difficulty of actual exam is 10x higher.

Most of the questions are trying to be tricky and really test that whether you have tried to run all codes in the lecture python file. Very tiny things are asked, like the position of the graph generated. Be very careful in the exam. I got get 2 questions wrong due to careless.......  >.<

Let's try to give some examples.
a = [1,2,3,4]
b = [7,8]
a.append(b)
a[-2]
What is the output?(3/4/7/8)

Which of the following codes can select the numbers with larger than 50?
x = [20,70,100,120,10,80]
A. newlist = [t if t > 50 for t in x ]
B. newlist = [t if t > 50 else np.nan for t in x ]

We have the data in the layout of  AAA, BBB, CCC (from left to right, in same row)
Which code can produce the histogram of CCC?
A. axes1=plt.subplot(1,3)
axes1.hist(df["CCC"])
B. axes1=plt.subplot(3,1)
axes1.hist(df["CCC"])

Please make sure you know the expected output of norm.cdf(Z) / norm.ppf(Z) / 1-norm.cdf(Z) / 1-norm.ppl(Z)

There are so tricky ffill and bfill questions / loc and iloc questions. You need to be a good compiler yourself >.<

One question also requires you calculate the sum of residual squares given the data.describe() result (i.e. a summary table), of which it is definitely not easy if you just have 2 minutes to calculate.

The exam requires you to understand BOTH statistics and coding, without either one you cannot answer the questions. Only 4-5 questions out of 30 is pure coding questions. All others you have to combine with statistical knowledge.

A lot of people say that the syllabus of this course is useless. This is utterly wrong. These are all very practical content for any kind of data science and analysis.

The only issue is that there are only 5 weeks to teach, so they only talk about the basics. As a result, people may get confused to what they actually are without prior knowledge.

I would recommend you to search online to gain more insights instead, but as an introduction course it serves its purpose.
sections.teaching:
I saw that a lot of posts claimed that Professor Wan has terrible handwriting and horrible delivery. This is partially true.

Indeed, his handwriting is quite bad and his delivery throughout is not very fluent, but understandable. More importantly, to compensate this, he gives out a lot more examples in the teachings.

Moreover, his notes are actually on point and relevant if you extract carefully. He is also the rare type of professor who provides final review and past paper exercises for you to do, which is extremely practical. He is also willing to answer any questions.

I would say he is a professor that prefer writing than saying, and he is definitely passionate in the teachings. If you have any questions, then ask him or search Google first. I do not think he is in any way bad given his notes quality and teachings.

He also cut the syllabus on point to save time, given that he spent a lot of time in Topic 0, which is just introduction.

For the Lab Session, I got Yvonne Chan. Her job is to basically talk about the code and give you an understanding of it.

Now, I do not know who write the code, but there are simpler expressions obviously and the most relevant code such as feature selection is hidden in another file. So, it is not easy to teach these code especially when people don't know much of Python. However, Chan has tried her best to invigorate your interest and answered any questions as well as give you more understanding about the code. I think she has done her job.

sections.content: The course is poorly designed to be fit in a 6-week course. This course is even tougher than ISOM 2500 (which is a 3-cred semester-length course) From multivariable linear regression model to model selection and different probability theorems, it is absolutely too tough for Year 1 students to follow through. It should have been a 3-cred course like ISOM 2500 and with sufficient guidance throughout the semester.
sections.teaching: The lecturer teaches quite well despite the horribly designed course structure. He tries very hard to deliver all messages and cover all topics within merely 2 hours in each of the 6 weeks. The TAs are also friendly and willing to answer your questions if you encounter any in doing the group assignment. Yet, the class is really in a rush so lecturer usually cannot handle too much queries in class.
sections.grading:
10% attendance
40% assignment (4 in total, 10% each)
50% final exam

Basically everyone knows they need to attend class, so 10% for everyone. Assignments are to be completed in a group of at most 3 (no assigned groupings), you can allocate workload among your teammates. Moreover, according to observations in Canvas, basically as long as you have done the assignment properly, full marks will be given. So most of the students get these 10%+40%. The grade is determined by final exam. The exam is rather difficult so you no need to worry about high mean (the mean is about 70% only), and finally, the grading is really lenient.
sections.workload:
The workload is very heavy. Within the 6 weeks, 4 group assignments have to be completed. All assignments are to use Python and panda libraries provided to complete the tasks correspond to the topics discussed in class. (linear regression model, best model selection, reasoning, etc) Working time depends on the style and ability of your groupmates. As each person can have their own programming style, it might be a tough work if you divide the assignment into 3 parts for each one to complete.

P.S. My group turns out to be one person doing Assignment 1, 2, another doing Assignment 3 and the last one doing Assignment 4, which I think is the most efficient way.

It is like an advanced course of ISOM 2500 in terms of data analytics, except it is infused with python coding skills.

(not much coding skills really as all you need to do is copy and paste the TAs' codes into your own program, change the variables and that's all)
sections.teaching:
Prof. Kris Pan is very good. Although she just read out the lecture slides during lectures, she would also give some notes and explanation on the contents. Most of the professors would have a QnA session before the exams as well to clarify our concepts. TA (Isaac <3) is very good as well, feel free to discuss philosophy with him in tutorials.

However, communication between profs and TAs & the bridging between previous IS courses are VERY BAD. In lectures, you will hear the professors keep saying 'This is taught in ISOM 2500' (but I don't remember ISOM 2500 teaching the stuff she mentioned) and 'This will be taught by the TA in the tutorial'. Then, the TA will be like 'I don't know what to do as well' as they just know how to code and nothing else regarding the lecture contents.
sections.grading:
the grading consists of assignments, participation and final exam.

Participation: just attend 5 out of 6 lectures (2% for each lecture), everyone gets them. For Prof. Pan, you are required to turn on your camera as well (online semester)

Assignments: 4 assignments (4x 10%). It is a group-project assignment. You can get all the codes required to solve the assignment by downloading all the files written by the TA during the tutorial. Change the variables and you should get the desired output and write some analysis and interpretation of the data based on your program. Remember to find some good teammates or else you will have to work on everything yourself with the free-riders.

Final Exam: 50% of the entire grade. All the professors will give out a sample paper before the exam, and the difficulty is more or less the same compared to the actual paper. (Prof. Pan was kind enough to have chapter review exercises as well but they are very basic) I find the exam to be quite hard and barely finished the paper within the time limit.
sections.workload:
Very Demanding for a 1 credit course. the workload and difficulty of the course are much more than a 3-cred ISOM 2500. The assignments are a bit complicated especially when you don't know anything about pandas and the different packages of python. The knowledge taught in ISOM 2020 is definitely not enough to understand the code and the logic of the code written by the TAs.

The lectures part are not very difficult given you really spend time on it. Be prepared that it is not as easy as ISOM 2020 and you really need to understand the topics and the theories behind the contents.

sections.content:
Look at "Course Outline 2020" for lesson details.

Overall, I found this course difficult. It is harder than even both prerequisite courses, ISOM 2500 and ISOM 2020, combined. Covering all this content in half a semester is plainly preposterous. This part should be especially reworked.

Logic behind the theories and concepts make sense after looking at the lessons over and over again. I am not mathematically-gifted and I hate statistics with a burning passion.

It doesn't help that those taking this course in spring semester are from Pathway 2 so they are typically more proficient in math, and I traded my soul for a decent grade in this course.  :)
sections.teaching:
Kris is, without a doubt, a very good professor. She explains in a clear manner and offers to answer questions in Cantonese, English, or Mandarin. She also offers reasonable explanations and can easily give you that aha! moment to understand the concepts.

Lab teaches the part on coding the statistics (the lessons) into Python. "Teaches" is a compliment that the labs don't deserve. Trust me, you only need the files with the code for the lab. Skipping the weekly 50 minute lab has no effect whatsoever on the final exam (which doesn't use Python) or the assignments.
sections.grading:
Components:
[40%] 4 weekly coding+stat assignments
[10%] Attend 5 out of 6 videos with video on 80% of the class
[50%] Final exam

My Scores:
Assignments out of 100 (100,98,100,100)
Attendance (full)
Final: 88/130 (mean: 77.9/130, sd: 23.1)

Scored B+ for this course and let me just say, the effort isn't worth the grade. In this sense, this course can be a blessing or a curse - a blessing if you mess up or a curse if you try so hard to understand the syllabus and use up time for other more important courses. At least I'm done with this course.
sections.workload:
Absurd. The weekly assignments make you disregard the time that should be allocated for courses with more weighting. Additionally, you just copy and slightly tweak the codes for the prompts given in the assignments. But then, I tried to understand the meaning of the codes and this consumed weekends. By the end of the course, you'll learn only to copy paste codes and not exactly code the statistics from scratch because it's too long.

Assignments are weekly and done in groups of 3, and you're free to choose your groupmates. With most scoring well (90+) in assignments, it doesn't matter though. The final exam had crazy time pressure. When I scanned the questions upon receiving it, I knew I wouldn't finish. I didn't even know if I typed the equation free from errors in Excel. I couldn't even read the questions properly.

For 1 credit, this course takes the crown for most stressful course.

sections.content:
Someone else pasted the syllabus already, I am not gonna repeat. Tho many may not agree, I think that the content itself is pretty good. We can learn both concepts and try to code it out and give interpretation, making the course pretty practical. I think the content is quite like ISOM 3400.

However, the downsides of this course is that the content was too much for a one credit course, and it should be extended to a full semester duration instead of only half. Since there are only 6 lessons, the professor and TA(in lab) are always in a hurry, they just have time to introduce the terms, explain what it does and then rush through it, no mathematical derivation/proof, and no intuition explained.
sections.teaching: Very good. Professor Pan’s accent is not native but comfortable, she explains clearly and patiently answer the questions raised by students. She even made a Cantonese Q&A session where she spend hours on using Cantonese to teach again and answer questions. But again, it is not easy to follow her pace in lessons since the course schedule was tight and therefore she taught really quickly, I think it was not her problem tho.

sections.workload:
The worst part of this course. If the workload in ISOM2020 is 1.5 credit, this course is ~3.5 credits, even the workload of 2020 is so light compare to this course.

Personally, I spent ~2hrs on lecture, additional 2-3hrs on revising the lecture, take notes and replaying the lecture video, and then ~1.5hr on learning the lab code, finally ~3hrs on the assignment each week! The assignments are difficult, they require you to be able to follow the labs to code, and then use your lecture concepts to explain/ interpret. What our group do was each do the hw once all by ourselves and cross-check. It was painful but it’s the only way that we get most out of this course.

To make this course better, they should increase the credit to 3 and make it last for the whole semester!
